key_insight: Dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings favor long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray process control can help reduce coating defects on Q235 steel, but wear performance should be evaluated at service-relevant humidity.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Characterize droplet morphology and coating microstructure.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and sliding wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates as humidity increases, without numerical results.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify humidity ranges or test durations, limiting direct translation to service conditions.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
